summary: Regression testing covered public lessons, registration/session refresh/logout, admin login, reset/change-password, quiz/progress, mobile layout, manifest, and active service worker. Most flows pass; brute-force lockout is not effective through the public endpoint.

critical.issue: After five sequential invalid-password responses (401) for the same test email, a subsequent valid login returns 200 instead of temporary 429 lockout. Backend logs show requests arriving from changing client IPs, while lockout key includes request.client.host, so the required public IP/email pair is not consistently tracked.

action_items: Make login-attempt identity stable behind the proxy (use trusted forwarded client IP handling or email/IP normalization) and verify five-failure lockout on the public URL.
critical_code_review_comments: Lockout currently relies directly on request.client.host; public proxy requests are observed from different 10.219.x.x client addresses, allowing the same email to bypass the intended IP/email counter.
seed_data_creation: Created uniquely named temporary learner accounts for lockout and reset tests; no seeded data modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Core API regression (lessons, registration, refresh rotation, quiz idempotency, progress, reset/change password) passed. Admin credentials passed. Mobile home/lesson navigation and navigator.serviceWorker.controller passed. Lockout remains unresolved on public ingress.
rca of the issue: server.py builds identifier as request.client.host plus lowercased email. Logs show the public ingress forwards requests with varying internal client hosts, so failures are split across login_attempts records. Use a stable trusted proxy header or define the intended identity semantics explicitly before counting attempts. No APIs were mocked.
